text: In this activity, we will be performing classification in KNIME.
First, we will create a new workflow and import our weather data.
Next, we will remove the missing data and then create a categorical value for the humidity measurements.
We will then examine summary statistics of the data before and after the missing data was removed.
And finally, build a decision tree workflow.
Let's begin. First, let's create a new workflow. We'll call it classification.
Next, we'll import the daily weather data using the file reader node.
Configure the file reader node to use daily underscore weather dot CSV.
Next, we'll add a MissingValue node to remove the missing values in the daily weather data.
We'll configure MissingValue to remove all the missing values.
Next, we'll use the NumericBender node to create a categorical variable for the humidity at 3 p.m.
We'll add the NumericBender node, we'll connect it to missing value,
we'll select the relative humidity 3 p.m. column, and we'll create two bins.
The first bin we'll call humidity underscore low,
That value will go up to 25.
The second bin we'll call humidity underscore not underscore low.
We'll check the append new column and we'll call the new column low underscore humidity underscore day.
Next, we'll examine some summary statistics both before and after we've removed the missing values.
We'll add the Statistics node to the canvas.
We'll connect the first one to the output of the FileReader actor.
We'll add another one to the output of NumericBinner.
We'll change the name of the first one to be BEFORE FILTERING,
and change the name of the second one to AFTER FILTERING.
Let's configure the first one.
We'll change the maximum number of possible values per column to 1500.
We'll also add all the columns.
Let's configure the second statistics node.
Again, we'll change the maximum number of possible values
per column to 1,500, and we'll add all the columns.
Now let's run our workflow.
Let's view both statistic nodes to compare the outputs.
In the before filtering statistics, we can see that there are missing values.
However, there are no missing values in the after filtering statistics.
We can also compare the summary statistics for different measurements to see that they are similar values.
For example, let's take a look at air temp 9 a.m.
We can see that most of the statistics are the same, as well as the distribution of values.
In the after filtering statistics, click on the nominal tab, and we'll look at the low
humidity day categorical variable we created.
We can see that the samples are equally distributed between the two values.
Let's close these statistics views.
Next, let's add a Column Filter node.
We'll connect this to the output of Numeric Banner, double-click to configure the node,
and we will exclude Relative Humidity 9 AM and Relative Humidity 3 PM columns.
Click OK.
Next, we'll add a ColorManager node to the canvas.
We'll connect this to the output of ColumnFilter, double-click to configure it,
and we'll make sure that HumidityLow is red and HumidityNotLow is blue.
Click OK to close.
Next, we'll add the partitioning node to the canvas.
We'll connect this to the output of Color Manager.
Double click to configure.
We want to split the data into two partitions.
The first partition should have 80% of the data.
The second partition should have 20%.
To do this, click on relative percent and change this to 80.
We'll make sure Draw Randomly is selected, and check Use Random Seed, and change the seed to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Normally, we would not specify the random seed.
However, since we want repeatable results, we use a specific seed value here.
Click OK to continue.
Next, we'll add a Decision Tree Learner to the workflow.
We'll connect this to the top output of the partitioning node.
Double-click to configure and change the min number of records per node to 20.
Click OK.
Next, we'll add a decision tree predictor node to the canvas,
and we'll connect the bottom output of partitioning to the bottom input of the predictor.
Next, we'll connect the output of Decision Tree Learner to the top input of Decision Tree Predictor.
Now let's execute our workflow.
We can view the resulting classification rules by right-clicking on Decision Tree Predictor
and choosing either View Decision Tree View or View Decision Tree View Simple.
Let's do the first one.
This shows the first two splits in our decision tree.
We can expand each branch by clicking on the plus.
Let's close this.
Now let's look at the simplified view.
Again, we can expand the branches to see the splits in the decision tree.
Close this.
Finally, let's save this workflow.
We'll analyze the results of the decision tree model in the next KNIME hands-on.
Save the workflow by clicking on the disk icon.
